# Security & Privacy Requirements Quality Checklist: Staff Day View of Reservations

**Purpose**: Validate that the access, privacy, secrecy and read-only requirements of feature 004 are complete, clear, consistent and measurable before implementation (formal pre-implementation review gate).
**Created**: 2026-11-09
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [tasks.md](../tasks.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Access Control Requirements

- [x] CHK001 Is it explicit that both operations are staff-only, and is "staff sign-in" defined by reference to feature 001 rather than restated differently? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK002 Are the three credential failure classes (missing, malformed, expired) each defined, and is a tampered/invalid-signature token covered by the wording "invalid"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, Spec §US4.1]
- [x] CHK003 Is the check order (route match, sign-in, validation, not found) stated once and consistently in FR-014, FR-010 and US4.3? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK004 Is it specified what a signed-in but unauthorized caller receives, or is the absence of roles stated as an explicit assumption? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK005 Is the status code and body for an unauthenticated request to a non-existent reservation id defined so that existence cannot be inferred without sign-in? [Coverage, Spec §US4.1]
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements defined for how `GET /reservations/{id}` interacts with the existing `POST /reservations/cancel` path so a path segment cannot be mistaken for an id by an unauthenticated caller? [Edge Case, Gap]

## Secret Code Protection

- [x] CHK007 Does "secret code and its stored form" unambiguously cover the plain code, its hash and any derivative (prefix, length, comparison hint)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK008 Is the no-leak rule required for error responses and logs of these operations, not only for successful responses? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK009 Is the measurable criterion for SC-004 explicit about the statuses and the depth at which the code must be absent? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [x] CHK010 Is the rule that the secret code can never be reconstructed from a staff read consistent with the staff cancellation of feature 003, which needs no code? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009]

## Personal Data Handling

- [x] CHK011 Is the set of personal fields exposed (name, email, phone) enumerated, and is exposure limited to exactly those? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK012 Is the no-cache requirement specific about what must be forbidden (client and intermediary caches) and on which responses (success only, or errors too)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK013 Is there a requirement on what is written to logs when guest data is involved (for example the table-missing log line), or is the log content rule only in tasks? [Gap, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK014 Is the assumption "staff are trusted with guest contact details, no audit trail" recorded as an accepted risk with its boundary? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK015 Are personal data requirements consistent for a cancelled reservation (is contact data still shown after cancellation and for how long)? [Gap, Spec §US2.5]

## Read-Only Guarantee

- [x] CHK016 Is "changes nothing" enumerated for every stored artifact and side effect (reservations, tables, schedules, closed dates, holds, emails) with no omission such as claims or logs? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013]
- [x] CHK017 Can the read-only requirement be objectively verified as written, including what "full stored state" comprises? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008]
- [x] CHK018 Is the requirement that repeating a request has no effect stated for failing requests (401, 400, 404) as well as successful ones? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Input Validation & Error Behaviour

- [x] CHK019 Are unknown query parameters required to be refused on both operations, including `GET /reservations/{id}`, which defines no query inputs? [Gap, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK020 Is the handling of a repeated `status` parameter or an empty value specified, or deliberately left to the strictness rule? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK021 Is a malformed identifier consistently 404 (and never 400) in FR-008, US3.3 and the contract, and is the reason documented? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK022 Is the 500 behaviour defined so that an internal failure never exposes stored documents, stack traces or personal data? [Gap, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK023 Are the standard error codes and messages for 401 and 404 referenced to a single source rather than restated? [Traceability, Spec §FR-014]

## Table Name Display (Conflict Resolution)

- [x] CHK024 Do FR-004 and US2.6 ("name it had when it was assigned") conflict with the last assumption ("a renamed table shows its current name"), and is one rule chosen and applied everywhere? [Conflict, Spec §FR-004, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK025 Is the last assumption placed inside the Assumptions list rather than as a stray item after it, and is its normative strength (assumption versus requirement) intended? [Ambiguity, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK026 Is the display value required when the table document no longer exists (for example "unknown") specified in the spec, not only in tasks? [Gap, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK027 Does SC-005 ("originally assigned table name") match the chosen rule if a table is renamed and then removed? [Consistency, Spec §SC-005]

## Documentation & Traceability

- [x] CHK028 Is it required that the documentation marks the secured operations and lists every response, including 401, with examples that contain no real-looking personal data or code? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015]
- [x] CHK029 Does every security requirement (FR-010 to FR-013) map to at least one measurable success criterion? [Traceability, Spec §SC-003, Spec §SC-004, Spec §SC-008]
- [x] CHK030 Is the constitution rule that JWT protects staff endpoints only reflected so that no other public endpoint gains access to reservation data? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- CHK019, CHK024–CHK026 correspond to analysis findings G1, I1 and U1
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
